parts.text: Supervisor note — scrutinize two specific points before your verdict: (1) The provisioned hook denies write_to_file/replace_file_content/multi_replace_file_content UNCONDITIONALLY, but deep-research-report-2.md (lines ~145-168) documents an artifact-aware variant that reads the hook stdin payload's artifactDirectoryPath and allows targets under it while denying everything else. Since hooks.json is GLOBAL, an unconditional deny also blocks agy's legitimate native artifact writes into ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/ (implementation plans, walkthroughs, task tracking) in the user's own interactive agy sessions — that is core Antigravity UX, and the code comment's claim that global blocking "benefits" interactive usage does not hold for brain-directory targets, which are exactly the writes the validator accepts. Assess whether the hook must be artifact-aware (allow inside artifactDirectoryPath, deny outside) and whether that was verified live. (2) Verify the claimed live evidence that the tools: allowlist is NOT enforced (the disproof of the primary research recommendation) is recorded convincingly in WORK_SUMMARY.md, since it contradicts the written research and justifies the pivot. If either point fails, route back to implement with findings.
